cards.name: CC Kernel
cards.summary: Applies a custom 3x3 convolution kernel: every pixel becomes a weighted sum of itself and its eight neighbours. Depending on the nine weights it sharpens, softens, embosses or edge-detects the image.
use_for: subtle sharpening of soft archival or upscaled news footage
emboss / relief texture on maps, logos or currency for explainer backgrounds
edge-detect line-art look for stylised documentary transitions
gritty hyper-detailed look on trailer stills
avoid: weights that do not sum to the Divider brighten or darken the whole frame
strong sharpen kernels amplify compression noise and halos on low-bitrate social clips

params.name: 2 - L2
params.does: centre weight (column 2, row 2); default 1 with all others 0 = no change
params.typical: 5 for sharpen (with -1 on the four neighbours), 8 for edge detect (with -1 all round)

params.name: 1 - L2
params.does: left neighbour weight

params.name: 3 - L2
params.does: right neighbour weight

params.name: 2 - L1
params.does: top neighbour weight

params.name: 2 - L3
params.does: bottom neighbour weight

params.name: Divider
params.does: the weighted sum is divided by this; set to the sum of all weights to keep brightness
params.typical: 1 for sharpen/emboss, 9 for a 3x3 box blur of all 1s

params.name: Absolute Values
params.does: 0/1 checkbox: uses absolute results so negative edges also show bright

params.name: Blend w. Original
params.does: mixes the original back in (0-100)

cards.equivalent: Sharpen (fixed kernel only; Find Edges and Color Emboss cover edge/emboss; Premiere 2026 has no custom-kernel effect)
cards.scripting: Match name is 'CS Kernel' (not 'CC Kernel'). Weights are named '<column> - L<row>': '1 - L1' = top-left, '2 - L2' = centre, '3 - L3' = bottom-right; all -100..100. Absolute Values is a checkbox written as 0/1 (number, not boolean). Blend w. Original runs 0-100 here. Divider min is 0.01; a zero-sum kernel (edge detect) needs Divider 1 and renders mostly black with bright edges. Demo is an emboss kernel (weights sum to 1). Render-checked: the unit emboss (-2..2) only shows as a faint relief halo on 1080p footage viewed small, so the demo doubles every off-centre weight (-4..4).

verified.note: Doubled emboss kernel (-4..4) now reads as a clear colour relief at thumbnail size: bright rim on the lower-right and dark rim on the upper-left of the figures, stripes and a small round motif plus crunchy embossed texture on faces and flowers, much stronger than the old faint halo render.

cards.name: CC Toner
cards.summary: Remaps the image's luminance onto a ramp of user-chosen colours (duotone / tritone / pentone), like a darkroom toner. Shadows, midtones and highlights each take their own colour.
use_for: sepia or archival tint for historical flashback sections in documentaries
brand- or party-colour duotone backgrounds behind titles and lower-thirds
cold blue monotone for tension or investigation beats in explainers
stylised reel covers and trailer title cards
avoid: full-strength toning flattens skin tones on talking heads; use Blend w. Original for a subtle tint
highly saturated midtone colours read as a cheap filter on serious news footage

params.name: Tones
params.does: 1-based dropdown choosing how many colour wells are used; default 2 = tritone (Highlights / Midtones / Shadows)

params.name: Highlights
params.does: colour given to the brightest tones

params.name: Midtones
params.does: main tint colour
params.typical: #8C6A45 sepia, #1F6F8B teal, or a brand colour

params.name: Shadows
params.does: colour given to the darkest tones

params.name: Brights
params.does: upper-mid colour, only used in the five-tone mode

params.name: Darktones
params.does: lower-mid colour, only used in the five-tone mode

params.name: Blend w. Original
params.does: mixes the original colour back in (0-1 in this build)
params.typical: 0.3-0.6 for a subtle tint, 0 for a full graphic look

cards.equivalent: Tint (two colours only); Lumetri Color creative tint for subtler work
cards.scripting: Colour wells take '#RRGGBB'. Tones is a 1-based dropdown (1-5, default 2 = Tritone: Highlights/Midtones/Shadows). 1 = Duotone (Highlights + Shadows), 3 = Pentone (all five wells). 4 is a separator and 5 is Solid (read from After Effects 26.0); Solid has not been rendered. Blend w. Original is a 0-1 fraction in this build (harvested max 1), unlike CC Kernel's 0-100.

verified.note: Whole frame remapped to a cream / teal / navy tritone, a clear duotone-style toner look

cards.name: Change Color
cards.summary: Shifts the hue, lightness and saturation of one selected colour range while leaving the rest of the image alone. Used to recolour or mute a single object such as a shirt, banner or flag stripe.
use_for: shift a backdrop, banner or clothing colour toward the channel palette
desaturate one distracting bright colour behind an interviewee
quick colour-swap gags in satire reels
recolour a stock graphic element to match the explainer palette
avoid: wide tolerance on reds/oranges bleeds into skin tones
hard, chattering edges on compressed footage; raise Matching Softness
for precise isolation Lumetri HSL Secondary or a masked layer is cleaner

params.name: Color To Change
params.does: the source colour to select
params.typical: pick from the frame, e.g. #C83228 red

params.name: Hue Transform
params.does: hue rotation in degrees for the selected colour

params.name: Saturation Transform
params.does: saturation change of the selected colour
params.typical: -100 to fully desaturate it, +20 to boost

params.name: Lightness Transform
params.does: lightness change of the selected colour

params.name: Matching Tolerance
params.does: how far from the colour a pixel can be and still change (percent)

params.name: Matching Softness
params.does: feathers the selection edge (percent)

params.name: Match Colors
params.does: colour space used for matching

params.name: View
params.does: 1 = corrected image, 2 = grey mask of what is selected

cards.equivalent: Lumetri Color (HSL Secondary; Premiere 2026 has no Change Color effect)
cards.scripting: Color To Change is '#RRGGBB'. Hue Transform is degrees (-1800..1800). Tolerance and Softness are 0-100 percent. Invert Color Correction Mask (0/1) changes everything EXCEPT the picked colour. Always leave View at 1 for the final render. Demo targets reds/oranges (red stripes, skin) so the change is obvious.

verified.note: Reds and oranges (red stripes, foreground-block fronts, flowers, also skin) rotated to green while the rest stays put

cards.name: Change to Color
cards.summary: Replaces one chosen colour ('From') with a specific target colour ('To'), with tolerance and softness controls for how wide the match is. Unlike Change Color, the output is an exact colour rather than a relative shift.
use_for: turn a red banner, shirt or graphic into an exact brand / party hex colour
match backdrop colours between shots in a multi-cam explainer
recolour a stock icon or lower-third to the channel palette
colour-coded comparison shots (side A blue vs side B saffron)
avoid: Change = Hue keeps the original lightness, so a dark source never reaches a bright target; use option 4 for an exact match
too much Hue tolerance recolours skin and wood tones

params.name: From
params.does: colour to replace

params.name: To
params.does: replacement colour

params.name: Change
params.does: which components are replaced (dropdown)
params.typical: 1 (Hue) for natural results, 4 for an exact colour

params.name: Change By
params.does: 1 sets pixels to the target, 2 transforms them toward it (smoother)

params.name: Hue
params.does: hue tolerance (Tolerance group), raw 0-2 units (default 0.1)

params.name: Lightness
params.does: lightness tolerance (Tolerance group)

params.name: Saturation
params.does: saturation tolerance (Tolerance group)

params.name: Softness
params.does: feathers the matte edge, 0-1

cards.equivalent: Color Replace (Target Color -> Replace Color, with Similarity) / Lumetri Color HSL Secondary
cards.scripting: Hue, Lightness and Saturation sit under the Tolerance header but are flat properties, addressed by their plain names ('Tolerance/Hue' also resolves). Values are raw 0-2 units (defaults Hue 0.1, Lightness 1, Saturation 1); how they map to the % shown in the UI is not verified, so reason in raw values. The harvest shows a second header row also named 'Saturation' (the group end); a by-name lookup hits the real slider first. Softness is 0-1. View Correction Matte (0/1) shows the selection matte; keep 0 for render. Colours are '#RRGGBB'.

verified.note: Red stripes, foreground blocks and flowers swapped to blue and skin went blue-grey, other colours unchanged

cards.name: Channel Mixer
cards.summary: Rebuilds each output colour channel as a percentage mix of the input red, green and blue plus a constant. Used for channel swaps, custom black-and-white conversions and strong stylised colour casts.
use_for: custom-weighted black and white for archival or flashback segments (Monochrome on)
surreal channel-swapped looks for glitch transitions in reels
faux infrared / alien tones for trailer moments
pull a colour cast out of badly white-balanced event footage
avoid: rows summing well above 100 clip the highlights; keep each output row near 100 total
channel swaps on faces read as an error in serious news content

params.name: Red-Red
params.does: share of input red in output red (identity = 100)

params.name: Red-Green
params.does: share of input green in output red

params.name: Red-Blue
params.does: share of input blue in output red

params.name: Blue-Red
params.does: share of input red in output blue

params.name: Blue-Blue
params.does: share of input blue in output blue (identity = 100)

params.name: Green-Green
params.does: share of input green in output green (identity = 100)

params.name: Red-Const
params.does: flat offset added to output red (percent of full)

params.name: Monochrome
params.does: 0/1: output a greyscale image built from the Red-* row

cards.equivalent: Channel Mix (approximate: per-channel gain/invert only, no cross-channel matrix; Premiere 2026 has no Channel Mixer video effect)
cards.scripting: Names read '<Output>-<Input>': 'Red-Blue' = how much input blue goes into output red; all -200..200 percent. Defaults are identity (Red-Red, Green-Green, Blue-Blue = 100, rest 0). '-Const' rows add a flat offset. Monochrome is 0/1 (number); when on, the red output row (Red-*) is copied to all three channels for the grey result. Demo swaps red and blue so skin turns blue.

verified.note: Red and blue swapped: red stripes and flowers blue, foreground blocks purple, navy areas brown, skin cool lavender

cards.name: Color Balance
cards.summary: Shifts the red, green and blue balance separately in the shadows, midtones and highlights, like three-way colour wheels driven by sliders. Used to warm, cool, split-tone or neutralise an image.
use_for: teal shadows / orange highlights for trailer and reel-hook looks
neutralise a green or magenta cast in news or event footage
warm up interview shots in documentaries
cold blue grade for crime or investigation explainers
avoid: values beyond about 50 produce ugly casts in skin
with Preserve Luminosity off, colour shifts also change brightness

params.name: Shadow Blue Balance
params.does: blue vs yellow in the shadows

params.name: Shadow Red Balance
params.does: red vs cyan in the shadows

params.name: Midtone Red Balance
params.does: red vs cyan in the midtones

params.name: Midtone Blue Balance
params.does: blue vs yellow in the midtones

params.name: Highlight Red Balance
params.does: red vs cyan in the highlights

params.name: Highlight Blue Balance
params.does: blue vs yellow in the highlights

params.name: Preserve Luminosity
params.does: 0/1: keeps overall brightness while shifting colour

cards.equivalent: Lumetri Color (Color Wheels); Color Balance (RGB) only for a single global cast
cards.scripting: Nine sliders, each -100..100 (0 = neutral). Negative red = cyan, negative green = magenta, negative blue = yellow. Preserve Luminosity is 0/1 (number). Match name ends in ' 2' (current version).

verified.note: Clear split tone: warm orange-pink highlights and background with deeper, cooler shadows and higher contrast

cards.name: Color Balance (HLS)
cards.summary: Rotates the hue of the whole image and adjusts overall lightness and saturation with three simple controls. A basic, older form of Hue/Saturation's master controls.
use_for: quick global desaturation for muted documentary B-roll
animated hue rotation for psychedelic or glitch reel moments
saturation boost on flat stock footage
avoid: global hue rotation turns skin green or blue; only for stylised moments
Hue/Saturation or Lumetri give finer control for real grading

params.name: Hue
params.does: rotates all hues, in degrees (no limit, 360 = full turn)
params.typical: +-5..15 for tweaks; 0-360 animated for a cycle

params.name: Saturation
params.does: overall saturation; -100 = greyscale

params.name: Lightness
params.does: overall lightness

cards.scripting: Hue is an angle in degrees with no harvested min/max (values wrap every 360). Lightness and Saturation are -100..100. Hue/Saturation (ADBE HUE SATURATION) supersedes it for most work.

verified.note: Global 90 degree hue rotation: reds turned green, the cool background magenta, saturation pushed up

cards.name: Color Link
cards.summary: Fills the layer with a single colour sampled from a source layer (its average, median, brightest or darkest pixel and similar), blended over the original. Used to make graphics automatically pick up the colour of footage.
use_for: auto-tint a lower-third bar or shape to the dominant colour of the clip behind it
unifying colour wash over a B-roll montage
make glow or light-wrap layers pick up the background colour in composites
avoid: at 100% Normal it replaces the image with one flat colour
the sampled colour flickers on fast-changing footage; lower Opacity or sample a calmer layer

params.name: Source Layer
params.does: layer whose colour is sampled (layer reference)
params.typical: index of the footage layer; default samples the layer itself

params.name: Sample
params.does: how the colour is derived (1-based dropdown, 11 entries)

params.name: Clip (%)
params.does: ignores this percentage of extreme pixels when sampling

params.name: Stencil Original Alpha
params.does: 0/1: keep the target layer's alpha so text/shapes stay shaped

params.name: Opacity
params.does: strength of the fill (0-100)
params.typical: 30-60 for a wash, 100 for solid graphics

params.name: Blending Mode
params.does: how the fill combines with the layer (1-based list of 21)

cards.scripting: Source Layer is a layer reference: a script sets it with the source layer's comp index (0 = none); specs and demo_settings cannot set it, so the demo relies on the default (the layer itself, giving a 60% wash of its own average colour). Sample: 1 Average, 2 Median, 3 Brightest, 4 Darkest, 5 Max RGB, 6 Min RGB, 7 a separator, 8-11 Average / Median / Max / Min Alpha. Blending Mode is 1-21 with separators at 2, 9, 12 and 17 (1 Normal, 3 Add, 4 Multiply, 5 Screen, 6 Overlay ...; enum_labels). Both read from After Effects 26.0. Stencil Original Alpha is 0/1.

verified.note: A 60 percent wash of the frame average colour flattens contrast into a pale beige-grey veil

cards.name: Color Stabilizer
cards.summary: Removes flicker and brightness or colour drift over time by locking the colour at one, two or three sampled points (black, mid, white) to their values on a reference frame. Only has a visible effect on footage whose exposure or colour changes over time.
use_for: remove flicker from time-lapses (city, crowd or rally time-lapse B-roll)
steady auto-exposure pumping in phone-recorded event footage
even out brightness drift in old archival clips
avoid: sample points must sit on static areas; a subject moving over a point causes pumping
does nothing on a still image or a single frame

params.name: Stabilize
params.does: 1 Brightness (one point, the Mid Point; medium confidence), 2 Levels (Black + White points), 3 Curves (all three points)

params.name: Black Point
params.does: [x, y] layer pixel of a dark, static area to hold
params.typical: a shadow area that never moves

params.name: Mid Point
params.does: [x, y] layer pixel of a mid-grey static area

params.name: White Point
params.does: [x, y] layer pixel of a bright static area

params.name: Sample Size
params.does: radius in pixels averaged around each point

cards.scripting: Match name is 'ADBE Deflicker'. needs_input: it needs footage that changes brightness over time; on a single still frame it shows nothing, so there is no demo. Points are [x, y] layer pixels (defaults sit on the centre line at 20/50/80% width of a 1920 layer). The reference frame is chosen in the AE UI (the frame where it is set up); the harvest exposes no reference-frame property, so verify a scripted use with a test render (low confidence on that part).

verified.note: status needs_input: renders nothing on its own, so no frame was made

cards.name: Colorama
cards.summary: Turns an attribute of each pixel (intensity, a channel, hue and so on) into a phase and maps it through a colour wheel (the Output Cycle), giving gradient maps, rainbow cycles, thermal-camera looks or animated colour cycling.
use_for: false-colour / heat-map look for surveillance or 'intelligence' segments in explainers (a true thermal palette needs an .ffx preset; the default wheel gives rainbow false colour)
animated rainbow colour cycle on text or shapes for reel hooks (animate Phase Shift)
abstract animated backgrounds from Fractal Noise
psychedelic satire beats in political reels
avoid: the default rainbow on faces looks like a cheap 2000s filter
the Output Cycle wheel cannot be set from a spec; whether a scripted Use Preset Palette index reloads the wheel is untested, so rely on the default wheel or an .ffx preset

params.name: Get Phase From
params.does: which pixel attribute drives the colour mapping (1-based dropdown, 10 entries)

params.name: Phase Shift
params.does: rotates the mapping around the colour wheel, in degrees

params.name: Use Preset Palette
params.does: loads one of 35 built-in output cycles
params.typical: leave default unless a specific palette is verified

params.name: Cycle Repetitions
params.does: how many times the wheel repeats across the input range

params.name: Interpolate Palette
params.does: 0/1: smooth blend between palette colours (0 = posterised bands)

params.name: Matching Mode
params.does: restrict the effect to pixels near Matching Color

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: mixes the original image back in (0-100)

cards.scripting: Output Cycle is a custom property: not settable from a spec; 'Use Preset Palette' (1-35: 1 [none], 2 Alpha Ramp, 3 Hue Cycle ... 15 a separator, 16 Carribean ... 35 Sunset, enum_labels; whether a scripted change reloads the wheel is unverified, low confidence) or an .ffx preset for a specific gradient. Name collisions: the 'Modify' dropdown and the 'Output Cycle' custom value each follow a header with the SAME name, and a by-name lookup returns the header first, so set the Modify dropdown by its match name 'APC Colorama-0016' in a script, not by 'Modify'. 'Add Phase' and 'Mask Layer' are layer references (comp index, 0 = none) set by script only. Phase Shift is an angle in degrees with no limit (360 = one full cycle). Get Phase From: 1 Intensity, 2 Red, 3 Green, 4 Blue, 5 Hue, 6 Lightness, 7 Saturation, 8 Value, 9 Alpha, 10 Zero (read from After Effects 26.0). Checkboxes (Modify Alpha, Change Empty Pixels, Interpolate Palette, Composite Over Layer) are 0/1 numbers.

verified.note: Intensity mapped through the rainbow output cycle: strong magenta / green / cyan false-colour image

cards.name: Curves
cards.summary: Adjusts tone and contrast through a drawn tone curve for the combined RGB or each colour channel (and alpha). The standard tool for S-curve contrast, lifted blacks and per-channel colour tweaks.
use_for: S-curve contrast punch on flat phone or log footage
faded / matte look (lifted blacks) for nostalgic documentary sections
per-channel tweaks for teal shadows and warm highlights
matching exposure between interview cameras
avoid: the curve cannot be set from a spec: applied alone it changes nothing
steep curves cause banding in skies and gradients on 8-bit footage

params.name: Channel:
params.does: which curve the UI shows and edits (RGB, Red, Green, Blue, Alpha); does not change the image by itself

params.name: Curves
params.does: the curve data for all channels (custom binary value)
params.typical: set through an .ffx preset, not a value

cards.equivalent: Lumetri Color (Curves section; RGB Curves is not in Premiere 2026)
cards.scripting: needs_input: the curve lives in the custom 'Curves' property, which ExtendScript cannot set; a spec can only set 'Channel:' (note the trailing colon), which alters nothing, so there is no demo. To use it from AdobeBridge, save the wanted curve as an .ffx animation preset in AE and apply it through the presets list (ae_lib preset()); for spec-driven tone changes use Levels, Brightness & Contrast or Lumetri Color instead. GPU support is medium confidence.

verified.note: status needs_input: renders nothing on its own, so no frame was made

cards.name: Equalize
cards.summary: Redistributes brightness or colour values so they spread evenly across the full range (histogram equalisation). Pulls detail out of flat or dark images and gives a harsh, high-detail look at full strength.
use_for: rescue very dark or flat archival / CCTV footage so detail shows
gritty high-detail look on trailer stills
quick auto-levels pass before a manual grade
avoid: full strength looks harsh and noisy on normally exposed footage; lower Amount to Equalize
it re-evaluates every frame, so brightness can pump on moving footage

params.name: Equalize
params.does: 1 RGB (per channel, shifts colour), 2 Brightness (luminance only), 3 Photoshop Style (default)
params.typical: 2 or 3 for natural results, 1 for a stylised colour shift

params.name: Amount to Equalize
params.does: strength of the redistribution (0-100)

cards.scripting: Equalize is a 1-based dropdown (default 3 = Photoshop Style). Amount to Equalize 0-100. Results depend on each frame's histogram, so expect frame-to-frame variation on moving footage.

verified.note: Per-channel histogram stretch darkens and punches the frame: deeper darks, more saturated stripes and higher contrast
